method: Local Vite, in-app Chromium on RTX 4070; identical viewport/DPR, Night preset, animated default isometric view; 120 warm-up plus 360 visible frames, asynchronous GPU queries; repeatable development legacy/optimized paths.

changes: Fuse alpha-weighted bloom addition with colour output; retain original threshold, all five blur levels, kernels and four-sample scene AA.
Eliminate the unused second multisampled scene allocation and depth buffers on bloom intermediates.
Reject the already-dark back side of rectangular lights before LTC lookups using the same mathematical predicate as Three r180.
Prepare linear HDR shader variants asynchronously and upload textures in short batches before revealing the scene.
Demand rendering idles paused presets and hidden pages, while animation, live time, orbit damping, time transitions and delayed water reflections can request frames.
Make development profiling opt-in and exclude it and the legacy comparison switch from production.

visualComparison.method: Paused initial view, identical models, time and pixel budget; RGB absolute pixel difference excluding controls. Small shadow-cache settling and float rounding differences remain.

browserChecks.pausedLoopIdle: observed after startup, transitions and camera orbit

automatedChecks.npmTest: passed, including renderer state/blur/alpha checks and 12 GLBs with zero errors/warnings
automatedChecks.buildAdvisory: Existing Three/R3F chunks exceed Vite 500 kB advisory

limitations: Both versions reached approximately 60 FPS on the test GPU. This measures less GPU work, not an increase above the display refresh cap.
GPU timings vary with clock speeds and other desktop activity. The earlier original baseline was 5.76 ms; the paired final legacy run was 5.34 ms.
The 390 x 844 check validates viewport resizing and production rendering, not performance on a physical phone.
Startup preparation is implemented and verified visually; no numerical cold-download speed improvement is claimed.
The repeated optimized run measured 4.24 ms versus 3.88 ms in the first run; report the observed 20.6–27.3% range against the 5.34 ms paired baseline.
